Definition: from G4810 and μόρον (the mulberry); the "sycamore"-fig tree:--sycamore tree. Compare G4807.
BiblicalUsage: The sycomore tree is the one Zacchaeus climbs. He ran before, and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see Jesus, for He was to pass that way. A short man in a tall tree, waiting for the Lord to pass.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the climbing shows the seeking heart: Zacchaeus could not see over the crowd, so he climbed above it.
